entry.content:

New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) will enforce a new "Click to Cancel" rule starting October 1, 2026. The regulation requires businesses to provide a straightforward cancellation process that matches the method used for signing up, prohibits charging fees to return items received for free, and mandates clear disclosure of subscription terms and consumer rights.

This municipal rule is the first of its kind in the United States and addresses regulatory gaps left after a 2025 federal ruling vacated a similar FTC proposal. Businesses violating the mandate face civil penalties starting at $525 per violation and may be required to issue consumer refunds.
